Browser Storage

You might say

Keep this draft after refresh, but do not treat it as a database shared by every user.

Browser storage is a local web mechanism for keeping data in a person's current browser.·It can remember dark mode, an unsubmitted form draft, or recently viewed projects so a later page load may restore them. It normally belongs only to that browser and device; clearing data, changing browser, or switching device may remove it.

Where a draft lives and what happens on another device

The draft exists inside Laptop A's browser.

What browser storage is suitable for

Local preferences and short-lived work: Theme selection, an unfinished draft, and non-sensitive interface preferences can remain in the browser so a page quickly restores recent work.

Its scope is usually one browser: It does not automatically sync to another device or make the data available to another user. Important information must also account for data clearing, private mode, and capacity limits.

What it is not

Browser storage is neither a server database nor a vault for secrets. A database supports server control, shared access, and more dependable persistence; information sent to a browser may be viewed or cleared by the person using that device.
